<thought>Based on the ^13C NMR (four down‑field signals around 68–89 ppm typical for sp‑hybridised carbons) and the HSQC data (one CH attached to a carbon at 68.6 ppm), the molecule likely contains an alkyne fragment (C≡C). The remaining up‑field carbons correspond to alkyl groups, including several methyl groups. A reasonable way to describe the structure as “connected fragments” is to split it into an alkyne fragment and the alkyl fragments that are attached to it. The following SMILES strings represent those fragments and can be joined through the alkyne bond to give a C10H13 skeleton consistent with the provided data.</thought>
<final_answer>['C#C', 'CC(C)(C)C', 'CC']</final_answer>
